executivePulse.interpretation: The situation in memory and AI infrastructure remains strained. Enterprise SSD, Server DRAM / RDIMM and HBM are currently among the most constrained areas. The Daily Check of 2026-08-18 reviewed eight current relevant reports; it does not indicate any confirmed material change in direction. New capacity and improved yields can relieve pressure, but will reach the market only with a time lag. For buyers, securing supply, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain decisive.

signals.title: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von Reuters: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.analysis: The report alters the build-out trajectory for AI and data-centre infrastructure. Increased productive compute capacity will pull demand for server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power delivery.

signals.title: Liquid Cooling Becomes Standard for High-End AI Infrastructure, with Penetration Expected to Reach 53% in 2026, Says TrendForce
signals.summary: Liquid cooling penetration among AI chips is projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and approach 60% in 2027. High-end chips from NVIDIA, AMD, and Google are driving the adoption of liquid cooling. NVIDIA’s rack-scale solution shipments are expected to double in 2026, while more than 80% of Google’s AI servers already use liquid cooling.
signals.analysis: The report is relevant for data-centre storage: it can affect prices, available capacities and procurement strategy for enterprise SSDs.
